# Shop placement audit — game signs vs. reality

**Part A (research-census): truth = OSM-surveyed + verified addresses, audit of the map data, before/after, rules, real street order.** Parts B/C (data: runtime sign dump vs OSM, pipeline) follow after Part A.

Owner: research-census (ORDERS item 16, shared with data and research-shops). Generated 2026-11-21T13:53Z by `tools/census/09_placement_audit.py` → `10_placement_plot.py` → `11_placement_report.py`.
Audited map: **current main** `gk3/kifisia_map.json` built 2026-11-21T13:49:43Z from census 202611211336; "before" = the map built 2026-11-21T08:50 (census 202611210845). Truth: OSM (kif.osm) + census.json 202611211349.
Machine-readable result for the pipeline: **`gk3/data/placement_audit.json`** (one record per game sign: truth facade, delta, flags, action). Anyone can re-run the audit on any map: `python3 tools/census/09_placement_audit.py <map.json> [--out=audit.json]`.

## 2. What "real" means here

| truth kind | signs now | how the real position is known | tolerance |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `osm` | 352 | OSM node/way surveyed by mappers (the raw point in the map POI, or the OSM object the census links to), carried perpendicular onto the street-facing edge of the building that contains it (or the nearest building within 15 m), preferring edges that face its `addr:street`. An OSM *building* (way) is right on any frontage of that building. | **4 m** (the order's threshold) |
| `address` | 111 | census tier A with street + number and two independent listings or a web/vrisko confirmation; position = census best position (OSM > house-number geocode on odd/even sides > Foursquare > Overture) | max(4 m, census `posErrM`); judged on **building, street and side**, not on the exact point |
| `single` | 106 | census tier B: one fresh listing; position = census best position | same as `address`; flagged SINGLE_LISTING |
| none | 0 | no listing in OSM or census tiers A/B | flagged UNVERIFIED |

Flags (a sign can have several): **DUPLICATE** (same OSM id, same census entry, or same normalised name within 60 m as another sign; the copy nearest to the real place is kept, OSM-sourced signs always win),
**WRONG_SIDE** (across the street from the truth; judged only when the truth side is reliable: OSM, house-number geocode, or error ≤ 12 m), **WRONG_STREET** (faces another street although the truth building has a frontage on the address street),
**WRONG_BUILDING** (not on the truth building and farther than the tolerance), **SHIFTED** (OSM: same building but > 4 m along the facade; address: farther than its error),
**ON_OSM_BAY** (a non-OSM sign covers the truth facade point of a displaced OSM shop), **CLOSED** (census tier X / open = false), **UNVERIFIED**, **SINGLE_LISTING**, **MISSING**.
Deltas are game sign facade point → truth facade point (for OSM the raw node often lies 2–8 m inside the building, so the raw distance would overstate errors).

## 3. What was wrong in the 08:50 map (diagnosis that drove data's v3.1 rebuild)

1. **70 duplicate signs** — the same business drawn twice, the second copy often 50–360 m away (Tommy Hilfiger, Vintage Lovers, Swarovski, The Body Shop, Eye-Q, Sparkle boutique, Advanced Plastic Surgery…): Overture records not matched to the OSM/census record of the same shop.
2. **OSM-surveyed shops pushed off their spot (78 > 4 m)**: bays packed along each facade in a fixed order, so on crowded facades (Kolokotroni block b33, b443/b444, Argyropoulou b492/b495, Kifisias b301/b305) surveyed shops slid along the frontage or round the corner, and unverified/single-listing signs took their place.
3. **Stale census positions**: that map used census 202611210845, before the house-number geocoder fix (Kifisias even numbers 244–256 had been 300–380 m off); a cluster of ~30 signs (Serras Flowers, BOMBERG, Advanced Hair Clinics…) sat on one Kifisias building 230–390 m south of their addresses.
4. **Nearest-free-facade snapping**: signs went to the nearest free street-facing edge within 45–90 m, regardless of the address's street and side (45 wrong street, 12 wrong side).
5. Census fix made in this round (13:35, census 202611211336, which v3.1 uses): a web entry geocoded from its own address no longer counts as an independent position (Zara/Sephora had "agreed" with themselves); when the preferred source disagrees with the address, a source that agrees with the address is taken; raw points are snapped to the side of the street given by the house-number parity (e.g. American Vintage, Levidou 5 → west side; Sephora stays at Levidou 8 east side, x 139.8 z 2.5).

## 5. Pipeline rules (for data — build_map3.py) and acceptance test

Use `gk3/data/placement_audit.json` directly: every sign has `tf` = truth facade `{b, e, t, fx, fz, faces}` and `action` (`keep`, `keep_if_free`, `move_to_truth`, `move_to_truth_if_free`, `merge_into:<id>`, `move_off_osm_bay`, `drop`, `drop_or_plate`); `missing[]` lists real businesses without a sign, with their `tf`.

1. **OSM first, exactly where surveyed.** Each OSM shop's bay centred on its `tf` (b, e, t). If bays collide, shrink widths (min 3 m) or move the *non-OSM* neighbour; an OSM bay never moves more than 2 m. If a building's frontage cannot hold all its OSM shops, put the surplus on a directory plate at the door — never round the corner onto another street.
2. **Then verified addresses** (`truth.kind == "address"`): on the frontage of `tf.b` that faces `truth.street`, on the side given by house-number parity, ordered by house number between the OSM neighbours.
3. **Single listings**: only on frontage of their truth building (or a neighbour on the same side of the same street within their `errM`) that is still free after steps 1–2; otherwise a plate/directory entry. Never on an OSM bay.
4. **Duplicates**: one sign per business. 5. **Closed** and census tier C/X: not built; **UNVERIFIED**: no shopfront.
6. **Never the wrong side or the wrong street**: reject any facade candidate across the street from `tf` or facing a different street than `truth.street`.
7. **Acceptance** before integrating: `python3 tools/census/09_placement_audit.py <candidate map>` → DUPLICATE 0, WRONG_SIDE 0, WRONG_STREET 0, CLOSED 0, OSM > 4 m only where step 1 fell back to a plate (listed). Current main: DUPLICATE 0 (met); WRONG_SIDE 1 (NOT met); WRONG_STREET 0 (met); CLOSED 0 (met); OSM > 4 m 53 of 352.

## Limits (honest)

- "Real" for non-OSM shops is an address-level position (10–30 m). The audit judges those on building, street and side, not on the metre. Exact unit boundaries inside a building are not in any open source.
- OSM nodes are mapper placements: usually on or just inside the right shopfront, occasionally at a building centroid; a few OSM shops may have closed since they were mapped (OSM has no reliable closure data here).
- Kyriazi house numbers are sparse in OSM (3 exact numbers); positions of Kyriazi 30–40 listings (Zara, Gap, Sugarfree, eyeQ, Kiko) carry ±15–30 m.
- The audit checks the map data the renderer reads (`MAP.pois` facade points). Whether `31_shopfronts.js` draws each bay exactly there is the buildings/data runtime check (ORDERS item 16).

## 7. Per-shop verification, street by street (OWNER DIRECTIVE 13:05: "go one by one")

Every shop sign in the core streets, plus every real business without a sign and every sign removed since the 08:50 map. One table per side of the street, rows in **real order** (`s` = metres along the OSM street axis; real position carried to its facade). `game #` = rank of the sign in the game's order on that side (a non-monotone column = an order swap). Address source: [web] = the shop's own site / brand store locator, [vrisko.gr] = Greek yellow-pages listing, OSM = surveyed by OpenStreetMap mappers, Foursquare / Overture = open place datasets (Overture sub-source in brackets). No Google Maps / Street View data is used.

**Status**: `verified` = drawn where the cited sources put it (OSM within 4 m of its shopfront, or a verified address within its error on the right building, street and side); `verified (moved)` = was misplaced in the 08:50 map and is right now; `misplaced → move` = still wrong (move to the real x, z); `unverified (weak listing)` = census tier B (one fresh listing, or sources that do not confirm each other), drawn on free frontage; `missing → add` = real (OSM or verified address) but no sign; `removed (…)` = was drawn in the 08:50 map, not any more (duplicate / closed / no listing / single listing) — `removed (VERIFIED - should be rebuilt)` means the removal was wrong.
